recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. It restores the published FHIR-13365 guidance to the datatype it governs, removes misleading Distance-local guidance, and does not require a new work-group decision.
issue_request: FHIR-13365 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3. It raised confusion between UCUM durations and ISO 8601 calendar-duration behavior in CQL/FHIRPath; the final resolution required date-issue guidance including leap seconds and a Duration usage note for whole-number durations resolving to natural calendar boundaries rather than adding a new unit code system.
initial_application: svn revision 12713, represented by git commit a236df77223290bcb12158e0302aa6c5aa163f63, corrected leap-second wording and added the requested whole-number duration note under Duration in source/datatypes.html. Later commit 0b0fbffb3b3f1d2e53f541470345ab8b7b3fc89a reordered Quantity variations and accidentally moved that note into the Distance rows while removing it from Duration.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists Duration and routes datatype pages through datatypes.html, so source/datatypes.html is current build-scope narrative. The Duration unit value set remains UCUM-based, which aligns with the modified resolution's guidance-only approach. FHIR-23564 later added a separate Duration semantic note, and the already-published FHIR-40624 reconciliation fixed headings in the same section but did not address this misplaced FHIR-13365 note. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later decision reversing the calendar-boundary guidance.
reconciliation: Changed source/datatypes.html so the whole-number Duration implementation note appears after the Duration usage row, removed it from the Distance subsection, and corrected the obvious typo from "1 month in is defined" to "1 month is defined".
source_changes: source/datatypes.html: moved the whole-number duration calendar-arithmetic implementation note from the Distance subsection to the Duration subsection and fixed the typo in the UCUM month parenthetical.
